eval.title: Amazon A Buy as Everybody Is Buying!

call.headline_quote: given the big guys buying it, it's not a bad addition to a portfolio now depending on how diversified you are

scenarios.name: normal
scenarios.quote: If I put 15% growth rates and then let's say it drops down to 10% going forward. If I expect a 10% discount rate P ratio goes down to 20 the intrinsic value is 179 180 not far from the current stock price.

what_is_priced_in.quote: Amazon is not priced as the market is is priced at an 8 9% return likely and that is why they are buying.

reasons.claim: At a 25 P/E with 10-15% growth continuing, Amazon looks cheap relative to the market and its own history.
reasons.quote: if the 10 to 15% growth continues, the P ratio of 25 is really cheap and that should bear fruit down the road

data_check.gap_note: he says 25, as-of 29.2887 (FY2025); annual vs TTM or a different definition

reasons.claim: AWS is reaccelerating and generating high operating margins, driving the growth thesis.
reasons.quote: AWS 24% growth. High operating income, that's 30 something% margin.

data_check.gap_note: not in our data: AWS revenue growth, AWS operating margin

reasons.claim: Heavy current capex will normalize down the road, unlocking large free cash flow that justifies today's valuation.
reasons.quote: let's say they hit 250 in 5 years the capex will not be 120 billion constantly maybe will fall to 70 and there you have 180 billion of profits that would justify the current valuation

data_check.gap_note: he says 2.5e+11, as-of 1.39514e+11 (FY2025); annual vs TTM or a different definition

reasons.claim: Amazon is a great, essential business given its dominant cloud and e-commerce position.
reasons.quote: It is a great business. It is an essential business now in the cloud AWS sector.

reasons.claim: US e-commerce market share is unusually high and likely to mean-revert lower as global competition grows, weighing on Amazon.
reasons.quote: the US market has 63% of market share. I think that that overtime will mean revert to the 50s somewhere and therefore that is a weight on Amazon.

data_check.gap_note: not in our data: US market share

external_facts_used: Druckenmiller, Klarman, Ackman and Buffett/Berkshire buying or holding Amazon shares
Bill Ackman's investment presentation citing largest cloud business by market share and 14% capital allocation to Amazon
Amazon's ~$200 billion recent capex commitment already booked
Sven's own research platform runs on AWS and has experienced occasional uptime glitches
US e-commerce market share estimated at 63%

critic.notes: Reason 5 reframes his 'US market share of the global world 63%' (likely US share of global equity market) as US e-commerce market share; that interpretation is not in the transcript. Stance matches: 'not a bad addition', personally passes, watch list.
